+//! Provenance: PR #3798 reporter hand-test; HTTP status meanings from RFC 9110 and provider API docs.
+
+/// The status of a cloud provider without a key. Test stays disabled while it shows.
+pub(crate) const NO_KEY: &str = "No key - Set API key...";
+
+/// The Ollama server address that the panel uses (no endpoint field yet).
+pub(crate) const OLLAMA_SERVER: &str = "http://localhost:11434";
+
+/// The model that Test and the status check use: the Model field like Send reads it.
+/// Spaces are trimmed. An empty field uses the provider default.
+#[must_use]
+pub(crate) fn resolve_model(input: &str, default: &str) -> String {
+    let typed = input.trim();
+    if typed.is_empty() {
+        default.trim().to_owned()
+    } else {
+        typed.to_owned()
+    }
+}
+
+/// The HTTP status in a transport error (`<host> answered HTTP <code>: ...`).
+fn http_status(error: &str) -> Option<u16> {
+    let rest = error.split("answered HTTP ").nth(1)?;
+    rest.get(..3)?.parse().ok()
+}
+
+/// One cause and one "what to try" hint for a failed cloud Test.
+/// `error` is the transport error; `http.rs` removed the key from it before and
+/// kept the provider's message, type, code and request endpoint in it.
+/// `endpoint` is the provider base URL (scheme, host and path).
+#[must_use]
+pub(crate) fn test_failure(error: &str, model: &str, endpoint: &str) -> String {
+    let lower = error.to_ascii_lowercase();
+    let billing = lower.contains("credit") || lower.contains("billing");
+    let status = http_status(error);
+    let (cause, hint) = match status {
+        Some(401 | 403) => (
+            "the provider rejected the key",
+            "Click Set API key... and paste a new key for this provider.",
+        ),
+        Some(402) => (
+            "billing or credits",
+            "Check the credits and the spending limits on the provider's billing page.",
+        ),
+        Some(_) if billing => (
+            "billing or credits",
+            "Check the credits and the spending limits on the provider's billing page.",
+        ),
+        Some(404) => (
+            "the provider does not know this model",
+            "Check the Model name on the provider's model list. Clear Model to use the default.",
+        ),
+        Some(400 | 422) => (
+            "the provider refused the request or the model name",
+            "Check the Model name. Clear Model to use the default.",
+        ),
+        Some(429) => (
+            "the rate limit or the quota",
+            "Wait one minute, then click Test again. Check the usage limits.",
+        ),
+        Some(500..=599) => (
+            "the provider is not available now",
+            "Wait some minutes, then click Test again.",
+        ),
+        Some(_) => (
+            "the provider refused the request",
+            "Check the key, the Model name and the billing.",
+        ),
+        None if lower.contains("not a valid model name") => (
+            "the Model name is not valid",
+            "Type a model name with letters, digits, '.', '-', '_', ':' or '/' only.",
+        ),
+        None if lower.contains("could not be reached") => (
+            "the network did not reach the provider",
+            "Check the network connection, a firewall or a proxy.",
+        ),
+        None => (
+            "the provider gave no usable answer",
+            "Check the network connection, then click Test again.",
+        ),
+    };
+    let code = status.map_or_else(String::new, |code| format!(" (HTTP {code})"));
+    let text = format!(
+        "Test failed: {cause}{code}.\nModel tried: {model} at {endpoint}.\nTry: {hint}\nDetails: {error}"
+    );
+    tracing::warn!(target: "camcraft::ai_settings", "{text}");
+    text
+}
+
+/// The Ollama status for a probe result. `test` marks a Test click, so the result
+/// always names the outcome and differs from a background check.
+pub(crate) fn ollama_status(
+    probe: Result<(), String>,
+    model: &str,
+    test: bool,
+) -> Result<String, String> {
+    let ready = |text: String| {
+        if test {
+            format!("{text} - Test passed")
+        } else {
+            text
+        }
+    };
+    let failed = |text: String| {
+        let text = if test {
+            format!("Test failed: {text}")
+        } else {
+            text
+        };
+        tracing::warn!(target: "camcraft::ai_settings", "{text}");
+        text
+    };
+    match probe {
+        Ok(()) if model.is_empty() => Ok(ready(
+            "Ollama is running. Type an installed model name in Model (see ollama list).".into(),
+        )),
+        Ok(()) => Ok(ready(format!("Ready (local model {model})"))),
+        Err(e) if e.contains("could not be reached") => Err(failed(format!(
+            "Ollama is not running at {OLLAMA_SERVER}. CamCraft does not start it. \
+             Start the Ollama app or run ollama serve. CamCraft checks again every 5 s."
+        ))),
+        Err(e) if model.is_empty() && (e.contains("HTTP 404") || e.contains("not found")) => {
+            Ok(ready(
+                "Ollama is running. Type an installed model name in Model (see ollama list)."
+                    .into(),
+            ))
+        }
+        Err(e) if e.contains("HTTP 404") || e.contains("not found") => Err(failed(format!(
+            "model {model} is not installed. Run ollama pull {model}, or type a name from ollama list."
+        ))),
+        Err(e) if e.contains("not a valid model name") => Err(failed(format!(
+            "the Model name '{model}' is not valid. Type a name from ollama list."
+        ))),
+        Err(e) => Err(failed(format!(
+            "the Ollama check failed for model {model}. Details: {e}"
+        ))),
+    }
+}

+## #3781 - Set up AI provider keys inside the app
+
+**What was decided:** Add a password entry field, save, remove, and test controls to AI Chat. Use the existing app keychain functions and the existing environment-first lookup. Saving replaces the provider's stored key. Remove deletes only the keychain entry. Clear the entry field after save, cancel, and provider changes. Do not return a stored secret to the UI.
+
+Run credential operations and readiness checks in background work. Show the key source as soon as the provider is selected. A ready status means that a key was found. An explicit Test sends a small request to the selected model and can incur a provider charge. Check local Ollama readiness and model availability as well.
+
+Explain API keys, provider setup, billing, environment precedence, and OS permission prompts beside the controls and in the user guide. Keep the PR a draft until the reporter confirms the macOS hand-test.
+
+**Why:** A desktop user must be able to set up a cloud provider without Terminal or an app restart. Reusing the existing storage preserves its service and account names. Background operations keep keychain prompts and network requests from blocking the UI. Distinguishing a found key from a successful test avoids a false claim about account access or credit.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** Environment-only setup does not work well for an app started from the Dock. Storing a key in preferences or the project would expose it. Displaying a saved key would create an unnecessary disclosure. Sending cloud requests automatically on provider selection could cause charges without an explicit action. A separate credential store would duplicate the existing platform support.
+
+**Cost to change later:** Provider instructions and links can change without a storage migration. Changing the keychain service or account names requires a migration for existing keys. Changing lookup precedence requires updates to the transport, readiness checks, tests, and guide.
+
+**Review fix scope:** Add the missing Ollama server commands and environment options to the panel and guide. Explain that a Gemini app subscription does not include an API key. Keep the current endpoint limit explicit. Track the live-ai smoke lane in #3803 and the distinct key-rejected status in #3804. Change this PR to reference #3781 because those requirements remain open.
+
+**Why:** The review permits a bounded fix with explicit follow-ups. The live lane needs real provider credentials and fixture tool calls. The rejected-key status needs provider error classification. Neither belongs in the Model edit scheduling fix.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** Do not claim that the full issue is complete or ask for the reporter's hand-test before the live lane runs. Do not add endpoint controls in this fix; #3783 tracks them.
+
+**Cost to change later:** The follow-up work can reuse the existing credential backend and provider transports. Its tests must preserve secret redaction.
+
+**Model edit scheduling:** Use a cloud readiness identity that excludes the model text. For Ollama, wait for a 500 ms pause in Model edits before checking the model.
+
+**Why:** A cloud readiness check reads the credential but does not use the model. Repeating it per character can show repeated OS keychain prompts. Ollama needs the model name, but a short delay avoids an `/api/show` request for each character.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** Per-character validation repeats credential reads and server requests. Checking only when the field loses focus delays feedback while the user stays in the field. A short pause gives feedback without requiring a focus change.
+
+**Cost to change later:** The delay can change without a storage migration. Backend-call-count tests pin cloud reuse and one Ollama check after the edit pause.
+
+**Reporter hand-test fixes (2026-11-24):** Test and the status check read the Model field as Send does: trim the spaces, and use the preset default when the field is empty. Disable Test while no key is found. A failed cloud Test names a cause from the HTTP status, the model and host that were tried, one "what to try" hint, and the provider's error text; the app log gets the same text. Test shows "Testing..." and a passed or failed result for Ollama too. A failed Ollama check runs again every 5 s, and an empty Ollama Model still tells if the server answers. The panel says that CamCraft does not start Ollama. The Anthropic help names the console choice "Somewhere else - Use an API key".
+
+**Why:** The reporter could not make an empty cloud Model work, a leading space failed Test, and a failed Test gave no cause. A status from before `ollama serve` stayed on the screen. The provider's error text is safe to show because `http.rs` removes the key value from it before it returns, for each provider's auth header.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** Keep the generic "Test failed" text: it gave the user nothing to act on. Re-check Ollama on each frame: it sends a request per frame. Start Ollama from CamCraft: it is a separate feature. Show the default model as the Model hint here: PR #3799 changes the same line, so this PR only resolves the default and names it in the Test result.
+
+**Cost to change later:** The cause table is one function (`settings_text::test_failure`) with a unit test for each class.

+An API key is a secret that lets CamCraft use your provider account.

+
+Choose a cloud **Provider**, then select **Set API key...**. Paste the key

+The field clears after save, cancel, or a provider change. CamCraft never
+shows the stored key. To replace it, use **Set API key...** again.
+
+The status appears when you choose a provider. **Ready (key from keychain)**
+or **Ready (key from environment)** means that CamCraft found a key.
+It does not prove that the key works or that the account has credits.
+**No key - Set API key...** means that you must add a key. **Test** stays
+disabled until CamCraft finds a key.
+Select **Test** to check access with a small request to the selected model.
+CamCraft removes spaces around the **Model** text. An empty **Model** uses the
+provider's default model. The result names the model that was tested.
+A failed test shows the cause (for example a rejected key, an unknown model,
+billing, a rate limit or the network), the model and host, what to try, and
+the provider's error text. The key is never shown. The app log gets the same
+text, so you can add it to a bug report.
+The provider can bill this request. Clear **Offline only** before a cloud test.
+**Remove** deletes the keychain entry only. It does not revoke the key at
+the provider or remove an environment variable.
+
+#### Get an Anthropic key
+
+1. Sign in to the [Anthropic console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys), then open **Settings > API keys**.
+2. Select **Create key**. Name it, for example, **CamCraft on my Mac**. This helps you revoke only this key later.
+   If the console asks **Where does your code run?**, choose **Somewhere else - Use an API key**. The other choices do not give a key.
+3. Copy the key at once. It starts with `sk-ant-`, and the console shows it only once.
+4. Paste it into **Set API key...** in CamCraft and save it.
+5. Keep it secret. Delete it on the same API keys page to revoke it.
+6. Check [billing](https://platform.claude.com/settings/billing) and [spend limits](https://platform.claude.com/settings/spend-limits) before use. Cloud requests use credits.
+
+See Anthropic's [API key instructions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/get-api-key).
+
+#### Get an OpenAI key
+
+1. Sign in to the [OpenAI API keys page](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys).
+2. Create a secret key. Name it, for example, **CamCraft on my Mac**.
+3. Copy it at once. Save the secret when the page shows it.
+4. Paste it into **Set API key...** in CamCraft and save it. Both OpenAI presets use the same key.
+5. Keep it secret. Delete it on the same API keys page to revoke it.
+6. Check [API billing](https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing/overview) and [limits](https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/limits) before use. A ChatGPT subscription does not supply API credits.
+
+#### Get a Gemini key
+
+A Gemini app subscription does not include an API key. Create the key in
+Google AI Studio with your Google account.
+
+1. Sign in to [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys).
+2. Create an API key for your Google Cloud project. Give it a name that identifies this computer.
+3. Copy the key and keep it secret.
+4. Paste it into **Set API key...** in CamCraft and save it.
+5. Delete the key on the same API keys page to revoke it.
+6. Read [Gemini API billing](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing). Check the project's billing and quotas before use.
